WPS_T|/layers/barrier/1: injection cream in a row of drill holes, holes resealed with {M30}
WPS_T|/layers/c1i/1: brush, trowel or spray into the matt damp substrate, free of pores
WPS_T|/layers/c1i/4: second coat after approx. 6 h ({AQ1KP}: 90 min)
WPS_T|/layers/c2i/1: when the first can no longer be damaged by reworking
WPS_T|/layers/c2i/4: third coat for pressing water, else curing
WPS_T|/layers/c3i/1: classic system: three layers for pressure water; > 3.0 mm in total
WPS_T|/layers/plaster/1: THERMOPAL-SP splatterdash, THERMOPAL-SR24, optional THERMOPAL-FS33 finish
WPS_T|/layers/repair/1: {BIS540} on {HSF} for voids, {BIS16} for the surface, felt finish (guide “Concrete restoration”)
WPS_T|/layers/tape/1: ASO-Dichtband-2000-S in {RB400} at the wall–floor junction and construction joints, no voids or folds
WPS_T|/layers/tape/3: ≥ 2.5 mm dry film over the tape
WPS_T|/layers/c1t/1: spray, brush or trowel over walls and floor, free of pores
WPS_T|/layers/c1t/2: approx. 1.1 mm wet per 1 mm dry
WPS_T|/layers/c2t/1: to the dry film thickness of the container class and the crack width
WPS_T|/layers/c2t/4: pressurised water after ≥ 1 day; keep damp
WPS_T|/layers/levelB/1: depressions > 5 mm with {M30}; highly absorbent substrates primed with ASO-Unigrund
WPS_T|/layers/tapeB/1: ASO-Dichtband-2000 tapes, corners and sleeves bonded in {AQ2K}
WPS_T|/layers/c1b/1: trowel, brush or spray, free of pores; even thickness with the notched trowel
WPS_T|/layers/c1b/5: A 2.5 : B 1, max. 0.5 l water / 35 kg
WPS_T|/layers/c2b/1: never more than 2 kg/m² in one step
WPS_T|/layers/tiles/1: laid with a tile adhesive of the system list (MONOFLEX, SOLOFLEX, UNIFIX-S3 …)
WPS_T|/layers/prim/1: {PRIM} where the substrate is extremely absorbent or slightly sandy; matt damp otherwise
WPS_T|/layers/prim/4: fully reacted before the scratch coat
WPS_T|/layers/scratch/1: {OS} pressed into the substrate as contact layer
WPS_T|/layers/scratch/3: in the total of approx. 5.5 kg/m²
WPS_T|/layers/c1p/1: wet in wet on the scratch coat
WPS_T|/layers/c2p/1: when the first can no longer be damaged
WPS_T|/layers/repairC/1: honeycombs broken out to sound concrete and filled, tie holes filled, the construction joint chased and filled with {M30}; cove at the wall–floor joint on a bonding slurry of {AQ1K}
WPS_T|/layers/repairC/3: approx. 1.4 kg/m² per mm; cove approx. 3 kg/m
WPS_T|/layers/presealC/1: {AQ1K} brushed into the matt damp concrete: the rigid slurry holds the moisture from the rear back from the flexible coating (RB400 data sheet)
WPS_T|/layers/bandC/1: {RB400} 15 cm on both sides of the joint with the 6–8 mm notched trowel, smoothed; two application steps
WPS_T|/layers/c1c/1: {RB400} by trowel or brush, free of pores; even thickness with the coating-thickness trowel
WPS_T|/layers/c1c/2: approx. 1.1 mm wet per 1 mm dry
WPS_T|/layers/c1c/5: A 1.5 : B 1, max. 0.24 l water / 24 kg
WPS_T|/layers/c2c/1: when the first can no longer be damaged; to the dry film thickness of WTA 4-6
WPS_T|/layers/c2c/2: ≥ 3.0 mm (water pressure), ≥ 2.0 mm (soil moisture) in total
WPS_T|/layers/c2c/4: keep damp ≥ 3 days in dry rooms; pressurised water after ≥ 1 day
RCP_T|/IC/role: The waterproofing of the system: brushed into the matt damp concrete in a minimum of two coats, its active ingredients penetrate the capillaries, react with the moisture and the free lime and fill the pores with crystals. Watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar, 14 bar on the positive side (CRD-C 48-92), suitable for drinking water, permanently active — it seals cracks of up to 0.4 mm that develop later.
RCP_T|/IC/areas/0: for waterproofing concrete containers, e.g. water tanks, sludge tanks and septic tanks
RCP_T|/IC/areas/1: for reliable waterproofing of concrete substrates
RCP_T|/IC/adv/0: seals cracks that may subsequently develop up to 0.4 mm
RCP_T|/IC/adv/1: can be applied to damp substrates
RCP_T|/IC/adv/2: penetrates the concrete via the capillaries
RCP_T|/IC/feat/1: suitable for drinking water after DVGW worksheet W-347 and W-270
RCP_T|/IC/feat/2: increased active crack healing in concrete
RCP_T|/IC/feat/3: CE after DIN EN 1504-2: surface protection material, moisture control (principle 2.2), reaction to fire A1
RCP_T|/IC/data/13/0: Consumption per m² and mm layer thickness
RCP_T|/IC/data/17/1: stirrer (approx. 500–700 rpm), mixing paddle, spray equipment, wide brush; machine application after Technical Information No. 43
RCP_T|/IC/data/18/1: cool and dry; min. 12 months in the original container
RCP_T|/IM/sub: Crystalline repair mortar for concrete, waterproofing
RCP_T|/IM/role: The repair mortar of the system: it fills the chased cracks, joints and holes flush, wet in wet on a screen of {IC}, and forms the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm at the wall–floor joint. Capillary active, with increased crack healing — the mortar takes part in the crystalline sealing. Suitable for negative water pressure.
RCP_T|/IM/areas/0: for water tight filling of open cracks and holes
RCP_T|/IM/adv/4: can also be used on damp substrate
RCP_T|/IM/feat/1: increased active crack healing in concrete
RCP_T|/IM/data/8/0: Max. layer thickness per application step
RCP_T|/IM/data/9/0: Consumption per m² and mm layer thickness
RCP_T|/IM/data/11/0: Consumption, coved fillet with 38 mm edge height
RCP_T|/IM/data/12/1: after approx. 1–3 hours wet in wet; after total hardening roughened first
RCP_T|/IM/data/14/1: stirrer (approx. 500–700 rpm), mixing paddle, trowel, flat trowel, brush
RCP_T|/IM/data/15/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 18 months in the original container
RCP_T|/F20/role: The plugging mortar of the system: pressed by hand into the dovetailed opening where the water runs, it solidifies after 1–2 minutes — even under water — with a clearly noticeable warming, and swells against the concrete. Under high water pressure it fixes the drain hose that relieves the pressure while the leak is plugged around it.
RCP_T|/F20/areas/1: for sealing water-bearing holes, cracks, fissures in concrete, masonry work and natural stone structures
RCP_T|/F20/areas/2: for the repair of concrete surfaces prior to the application of a surface waterproofing system (e.g. {IC})
RCP_T|/F20/areas/3: for fastening wall anchors and other assembly parts that must be able to withstand short-term loads
RCP_T|/F20/data/13/1: clean mixing bucket, protective gloves, trowel, flat trowel
RCP_T|/F20/data/14/1: concrete, masonry work, natural stone: firm, load-bearing, clean, free of adhesion inhibiting substances; the leak position chiselled to a dovetail
RCP_T|/F20/data/15/1: cool, dry, protected from sunlight; min. 12 months in the original container
RC_STEPS|/planR/title: Assess the water and the concrete
RC_STEPS|/planR/short: Water load sets the material rate; water quality, cracks and what may follow on the coating are checked first.
RC_STEPS|/planR/overview: The material rate of {IC} follows the water load: 0.75 kg/m² in one layer for soil moisture and non-accumulating seepage water, 1.2 kg/m² in two layers for non-pressurised water, 1.5 kg/m² in two layers for accumulated water. The slurry is watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar and to 14 bar on the positive side (CRD-C 48-92); it is suitable for drinking water (DVGW W 270, W 347).
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/0: static cracks and construction joints wider than 0.4 mm are opened to 20 mm width and 25 mm depth and repaired with {IM}; dynamic cracks are not filled with mortar
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/1: water ingress is stopped in advance with {F20} (or FIX 10-S plugging cement); voids are repaired with the ASOCRET-BIS system or {IM}
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/2: aggressive or soft water (hardness < 30 mg CaO per litre) always requires a water analysis; the degree of attack is evaluated in accordance with EN 1992-1-1
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/3: {IC} cannot be overcoated with tiles, plaster, bonded screeds or paint, and cannot be used as an additive to concrete or plaster
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/4: concrete with fly ash: discolouration or a reduced reaction may occur — contact the technical service; different colouring depends on the moisture content of the concrete
RC_STEPS|/planR/points/5: movement and connecting joints are formed watertight with ASO-Dichtband system components
RC_STEPS|/prepR/short: Firm, load-bearing, pore open, absorbent; smooth areas roughened; jetted at > 400 bar; wetted repeatedly to matt damp.
RC_STEPS|/prepR/overview: The substrate must be firm, load-bearing, pore open, free of adhesion inhibiting substances and absorbent. Smooth surface areas are mechanically roughened to achieve a good penetration depth. Less adhesive and bond-damaging substances are completely removed: high-pressure water jetting (> 400 bar; < 2000 bar) and jets with fixed blasting agents are suitable; the last step is cleaning with pressure water jetting.
RC_STEPS|/prepR/points/0: dampen the surfaces to be sealed with clean water beforehand; repeated moistening alters the absorption behaviour and favours the growth of the crystals
RC_STEPS|/prepR/points/1: the surface must be matt damp at the time of application; the formation of puddles must be avoided
RC_STEPS|/prepR/points/2: dense and smooth substrates for {IM} are roughened with sand, high-pressure water or shot blasting
RC_STEPS|/prepR/points/3: for {F20}: loose pieces of plaster and masonry removed; the leak position chiselled to a dovetail for better anchoring
RC_STEPS|/openR/short: Static cracks and joints chased to 20 mm wide and 25 mm deep; loose debris removed; leaks chiselled to a dovetail.
RC_STEPS|/openR/overview: Loose debris is removed from the cracked areas. Defective construction joints and visible static cracks over 0.4 mm are opened to a width of up to 20 mm and a depth of 25 mm so that {IM} can fill them flush. Where water runs out, the opening is chiselled to a dovetail shape for the better anchoring of the {F20} plug.
RC_STEPS|/openR/points/0: crack width 20 mm, depth 25 mm (system page: at least 20 mm and 25 mm)
RC_STEPS|/openR/points/1: the chased edges are screened with {IC} before the mortar goes in
RC_STEPS|/openR/points/2: voids and honeycombs are broken out to sound concrete and filled with {F20} or {IM}, larger ones with the ASOCRET-BIS system
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/short: Approx. 200–250 g of water per kg, mixed for at least a minute in small quantities: pot life approx. 2 minutes.
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/overview: Pour approx. 200–250 g of water per kg of {F20} with the powder component into a clean mixing bucket and mix to a homogeneous, lump-free mass. Solidification starts after 1–2 minutes and the pot life is approx. 2 minutes — mix only what can be placed at once.
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/points/0: mixing time at least approx. 1 minute; protective gloves
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/points/1: at low temperatures use warm water and pre-warmed powder; at high temperatures cool water and cooled powder — the powder must not exceed +23 °C
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/points/2: the material can be used as mortar or alternatively in dry form
RC_STEPS|/mixF20/points/3: appropriate preliminary tests must be carried out; {F20} must not be mixed with plaster or brought into contact with plaster
